overview.body:
**Krátos** ​(*kratos*) ‌— Strength, ‌Power, ​Sovereignty ​· ​Strength, ​power — ​belongs ‌to ​the ​Greek ‌tradition, where ​it ‌is ​catalogued ‌under the ​domain ​"Strength, ​Power, ​Sovereignty". ​The name ‌means ​"Strength, ‌power"[^1].

​**Krátos** belongs ‌to ​the ‌Greek ​tradition, ‌where it ​is ​associated ‌with ‌strength, ‌power, sovereignty.[^2]

​PuniCodex ​restores ‌the ​name as ​**Krátos** ‌and ​serves ​its ‌temple at ​[kratos.com](https://punicodex.com/kratos/). ‌The ​original ​preserves ​one prosodic ​feature ‌— ‌stress ​or vowel ‌length ​— ​rather ‌than ‌both, which ‌places ‌the ​name ‌in ​Tier 2. ​The ​plain ‌ASCII ​form *kratos* ​survives ​as ‌a ​modern ​convenience imposed ​by ‌the ​early ‌domain-name system; ​the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, is ​the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete[^3].

the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested in ‌Greek as ​**Κράτος**. ​Etymologically it ​means "Strength, ​power"[^1].

​The reconstructed ‌proto-form is ​*kret-* (proto-indo-european, ​"to ‌be strong"). ​Greek κράτος ‌'strength, power, ​might'; ‌personified as ​one of ​the ​children of ​the Titan ​Pallas and ‌Styx.

​The ASCII ‌form *kratos* ​survives only ‌because ​the early ‌domain-name system ​could ‌not carry ​diacritics; it ​is a ‌technological ‌compromise, not ‌an ancient ​spelling. The ​Unicode ‌restoration **Krátos** ​recovers the ​stress ‌accent of ​the original ​directly in ‌the ​address bar. ‌The original ​preserves one ​prosodic ​feature — ​stress or ‌vowel ‌length — ​rather than ‌both, which ​places ​the name ‌in Tier ‌2.

The ‌letter-by-letter ‌transformation runs:

​- **k** ‌→ ​**K** — ​Kappa
- ​**r** → ‌**r** ​— Rho
​- **a** ​→ **á** ‌— ​Acute on ​alpha
- ​**t** ‌→ **t** ​— Tau
‌- **o** ​→ ‌**o** — ​Omicron
- ‌**s** → ‌**s** ​— Sigma

​The canonical ​temple ​for this ‌name is ‌served at ​**kratos.com**[^2].

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation ‌of ​the ​name is ​**/kratos/** ​— ​Greek ‌Reconstruction.[^1]

​Phoneme ​by ‌phoneme:

​- ‌**K** ​— Initial ‌character ​of ​the ​restored ​form ​Krátos.
‌- ​**rátos** ‌— Remainder ​of ‌the ​name, ‌preserving ​the ‌distinctive ​marks ​of ‌the ‌Greek tradition.

‌For ​the ​modern ‌speaker, ​the ​closest ‌approximation ​is: ​'KRATOS' ‌— pronounce ​the ‌restored ​form ​with ​attention ​to ‌the ‌preserved ​diacritics ‌and length.

​Kindred ​and ‌historical ‌forms ‌of ‌the ​name:

‌- ​**Greek** ​— Krátos, ​the ‌restored ​Unicode ​form ​of ‌the ​name

​Krátos ​is Tier ‌2 ​because ‌the ​Greek ‌form ​preserves ‌distinctive ‌features ​that ​ASCII loses: ​stress, ​length, ‌or ‌special ​characters.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌**Krátos** ‌circulate ​within the ​Greek ​corpus, where ​the ​figure embodies ‌strength, ​power, ​sovereignty.[^1]

### ‌Primary ​Attestation (Sources)

‌Krátos ​is attested ‌in ​the ​canonical Greek ​sources ​as a ​figure ‌associated ​with strength, ‌power, ​sovereignty.[^2]

### ‌Name ​and Meaning ‌(Etymology)

​The ‌name means ​"Strength, ​power" and ‌reflects ‌the figure's ‌role ​in ​the tradition. ‌**Krátos** ​is the ​personification ‌of ​strength or ​sovereign ‌power in ​Greek ‌poetry. In ​Aeschylus's ​*Prometheus ​Bound* he ​is ‌the pitiless ‌agent ​who ‌compels Hephaestus ​to ​bind Prometheus, ‌embodying ‌the coercive ‌force ‌that ​even the ‌craftsman-god ​cannot refuse.[^1] ​Unlike ​his brother ‌Bía ​(Violence), ​Krátos represents ​institutionalized, ‌legitimate might. ​His ​pairing ​with Bía ‌in ​the binding ‌of ​Prometheus shows ‌that ​Greek ‌tragedy could ‌personify ​abstract forces ​and ​set them ​in ‌dialogue ‌with the ​gods.[^2]
